gloss: to transfer in; to move in (to a new jurisdiction)

definitions.gloss: to transfer in; to move in (to a new area or school)
definitions.explanation: To officially register as a new resident in a municipality, or to transfer into a new school. Used in administrative and educational contexts for formal relocation.

examples.japanese: {東京|とうきょう}から{大阪|おおさか}に{転入|てんにゅう}した。
examples.english: I transferred my residence from Tokyo to Osaka.

examples.japanese: {転入|てんにゅう}{届|とどけ}を{市役所|しやくしょ}に{出|だ}してください。
examples.english: Please submit the transfer-in notification at the city hall.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{学校|がっこう}に{転入|てんにゅう}したばかりで、まだ{友達|ともだち}がいない。
examples.english: I just transferred to a new school, so I don't have any friends yet.

notes:
An administrative term for officially moving into a new municipality or transferring into a new school. When moving between municipalities in Japan, residents must file a {転入|てんにゅう}{届|とどけ} (transfer-in notification) at their new city hall within 14 days.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {転入|てんにゅう}{届|とどけ}: transfer-in notification
- {転入|てんにゅう}{届出|とどけで}: filing of transfer-in notification
- {転入|てんにゅう}{手続|てつづ}き: transfer-in procedures
- {転入|てんにゅう}{生|せい}: transfer student
- {転入|てんにゅう}{者|しゃ}: new resident

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {転出|てんしゅつ}する: to transfer out — the opposite; officially leaving a municipality
- {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}す: to move (house) — the everyday word for physically relocating, without the administrative nuance
- {転校|てんこう}する: to change schools — specifically for school transfers
